text:
Jaroslav Chmelar is a 6-foot-5, 238-pound fifth-round pick who has spent most of his pro career in Hartford, and this fall he is making the Rangers notice. Forever Blueshirts described him as "on a mission," and he has backed that up with goals in back-to-back games: one against Seattle on Nov. 7, then a breakaway shorthanded goal at Edmonton two nights later.

He plays small minutes, about 8.5 a night, so keep the sample in mind. Two goals on 1.29 expected goals (the quality of his chances) is a bit ahead of the chances, and 25% shooting won't last. The forechecking side is real, though: 22 hits in 12 games, and his top skating speed ranks in the 90th percentile of the league, unusual for someone his size.

The concern is at five on five, where New York has 40.8% of expected goals with him on the ice, well below the team's level without him. His comparables make the role clear: physical bottom-six forwards whose value lies in energy and the forecheck. Watch whether he keeps a spot when the lineup is healthy.
headline: Chmelar is making the most of his minutes
